homage

OM-ij (or hom-AHZH) — to 'pay homage' is to publicly honor someone, the way a knight once honored a lord. · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Homage is special honor or respect shown publicly.

The retiring coach's former players returned from across the country to pay homage to him at his final game.

Example

A young chef opens her own restaurant and pays homage to the grandmother who taught her to cook by naming her signature dish after her, serving it exactly the way her grandmother made it every Sunday, right down to the same handwritten recipe card on the wall.

That deliberate, public tribute to her grandmother's legacy is what paying homage means. Unlike 'imitation,' which can be careless copying, homage is a respectful, intentional tribute.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

tribute: A tribute is any act or gift given to show respect — a speech, a plaque, a moment of silence. Homage is a particular kind of tribute: it bows to an influence, often by echoing the honored one's own work or style.

honor: Honor is high public regard or respect — a state you hold in people's eyes rather than a thing you do. Homage is an act, not a state: you pay homage through a deliberate public gesture that displays the honor you feel.

salute: A salute is a quick, visible gesture of respect — a raised hand, a nod to the crowd, a mention from the stage. Homage runs deeper and more deliberate: paying homage means crafting a real tribute, often by echoing the honored person's own work.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

insult: a disrespectful or offensive remark or action

mockery: ridicule or scornful imitation

Where it sits · how deep the respect shown runs — compliment → homage → reverence

compliment vs. homage: A compliment is smaller and more casual than homage — a compliment is a brief kind remark, while homage is a deliberate, often public tribute meant to honor someone's whole legacy.

reverence vs. homage: Reverence can feel even deeper than homage: homage is usually a specific act of tribute, but reverence describes an ongoing, deep-seated feeling of awe and respect.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — hom-/hum-

root — hom-/hum-: man, human being (Latin (homo))

Put it together

Put it together: Latin homo meant 'man, human being.' In medieval Old French, homage originally described the formal ceremony where a vassal publicly declared himself the 'man' (loyal servant) of his lord. Today, paying homage still means publicly, formally honoring someone.

Use the root in a new word: human

Use the root in a new word: human: Every human being deserves to be treated with basic dignity and respect.
